content: The provided text is extensive and contains detailed information about drug interactions, particularly focusing on entecavir and its interactions with various other drugs. 1. Entecavir Dosage and Administration: For patients with lamivudine-refractory hepatitis B or known resistance to lamivudine or telbivudine (adults and adolescents aged ≥16 years), the recommended dose is 1 mg orally once daily. For adults with decompensated liver disease, the recommended dose is also 1 mg orally once daily. Entecavir should be taken on an empty stomach, either 2 hours before or 2 hours after a meal. For patients with renal impairment requiring dosage adjustments, an oral solution is recommended. 2. Indications: Entecavir is indicated for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in patients with evidence of active viral replication and either persistent elevations in serum aminotransferases (ALT or AST) or histologically active disease. In pediatric patients aged ≥2 years and weighing at least 10 kg, safety and efficacy have been established. However, for children under 2 years of age, safety and efficacy have not been established. 3. Renal Impairment in Pediatric Patients: Insufficient data exist to recommend specific dose adjustments for pediatric patients with renal impairment. Dose reductions or increased dosing intervals, similar to adult adjustments, should be considered. 4. Drug Interactions: General Considerations: Co-administration of entecavir with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of either entecavir or the co-administered drug. Caution and monitoring are advised. Specific Interactions: Entecavir and Tenofovir DF: Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Monitor for toxicity. Entecavir and Metformin: Co-administration may increase the risk of lactic acidosis. Use caution and monitor closely.
